records.originalText: In Japan, chefs must take a special exam to be allowed to prepare pufferfish.
records.finalText: In Japan, chefs must take a special exam to be allowed to prepare pufferfish.
records.rationale: Reject this generalized regulatory claim: licensing requirements vary by jurisdiction and date; source ratings do not establish current factual scope.

records.originalText: I'm at a loss for words.
records.finalText: I'm at a loss for words.
records.rationale: Natural conversational idiom at a loss for words; idiomatic meaning rather than literal vocabulary sets the level.

records.originalText: What subjects are you taking at school?
records.finalText: What subjects are you taking at school?
records.rationale: Clear school question using present progressive for current studies; common school vocabulary.

records.originalText: Your marks were well below average this term.
records.finalText: Your marks were well below average this term.
records.rationale: Natural British English school marks; well below average and this term require intermediate reading.

records.originalText: What have you done with your car?
records.finalText: What have you done with your car?
records.rationale: Natural present-perfect question about the result of an action involving a car.

records.originalText: Could you lend me your bicycle for a couple of days?
records.finalText: Could you lend me your bicycle for a couple of days?
records.rationale: Common polite could request; lend and a couple of days in a concrete everyday situation.

records.originalText: Your idea seems to be similar to mine.
records.finalText: Your idea seems to be similar to mine.
records.rationale: Natural comparison with seems to be and possessive pronoun mine.

records.originalText: Local shops do good business with tourists.
records.finalText: Local shops do good business with tourists.
records.rationale: Idiomatic do good business with tourists, understandable as a local commerce example.

records.originalText: The manager sat on the bench with his arms folded.
records.finalText: The manager sat on the bench with his arms folded.
records.rationale: Grammatical past narration with with his arms folded describing posture.

records.originalText: The rock concert was called off because the singer fell ill.
records.finalText: The rock concert was called off because the singer fell ill.
records.rationale: Natural causal clause; review called off and fell ill as intermediate multiword expressions.

records.originalText: Who taught you to play the piano?
records.finalText: Who taught you to play the piano?
records.rationale: Natural past-simple who subject question with teach someone to play an instrument.

records.originalText: What if he should fail?
records.finalText: What if he should fail?
records.rationale: Reject the standalone fragment without an established referent or failure scenario; do not invent context.

records.originalText: I'll punch your lights out!
records.finalText: I'll punch your lights out!
records.rationale: Reject the violent threat even though the idiom is authentic and positively rated upstream.

records.originalText: A football team consists of eleven players.
records.finalText: A football team consists of eleven players.
records.rationale: Grammatical consists of phrase with a familiar football-team example.

records.originalText: While waiting for the bus, I was caught in a shower.
records.finalText: While waiting for the bus, I was caught in a shower.
records.rationale: Natural introductory while participle clause; caught in a shower means caught in rain in this bus-waiting context.

records.originalText: It was such a nice day that the street was full of people.
records.finalText: It was such a nice day that the street was full of people.
records.rationale: Natural such a nice day that result construction and everyday street description.

records.originalText: How shall I put it?
records.finalText: How shall I put it?
records.rationale: Reject this discourse prompt because it provides no subject to express or reformulate in an isolated typing example.

records.originalText: Would you be so kind as to open the door for me?
records.finalText: Would you be so kind as to open the door for me?
records.rationale: Natural formal request using would you be so kind as to.

records.originalText: The problem is beyond the scope of my understanding.
records.finalText: The problem is beyond my understanding.
records.rationale: Edit the cumbersome beyond the scope of my understanding to beyond my understanding; preserve difficulty/meaning.

records.originalText: All essays must be handed in on time.
records.finalText: All essays must be handed in on time.
records.rationale: Natural passive obligation with hand in for essay submission and a clear deadline constraint.

records.originalText: I hurt my eye when my contact slipped out of place.
records.finalText: I hurt my eye when my contact lens slipped out of place.
records.rationale: Expand colloquial contact to contact lens so the eye-related example is unambiguous when read alone.

records.originalText: This ship is not fit for an ocean voyage.
records.finalText: This ship is not fit for an ocean voyage.
records.rationale: Natural fit for and ocean voyage in a seaworthiness example; statement gives no navigation instructions.

records.originalText: These products are selling like hot cakes.
records.finalText: These products are selling like hot cakes.
records.rationale: Natural sales idiom selling like hot cakes; retain the established two-word spelling variant.

records.originalText: A holiday this summer is out of the question.
records.finalText: A holiday this summer is out of the question.
records.rationale: Natural idiom out of the question meaning impossible or not feasible.
